compound.name: chrysin
compound.one_liner: Simplest 4'-deoxyflavone; a biosynthetic precursor more than an abundant constituent (≤0.08 % of S. baicalensis root).

identity.note: Names-and-Identifiers heading URL was rate-limited (HTTP 429); values read from the full-record URL instead.

biosynthesis.note: Product of FNSII-2 in S. baicalensis roots and precursor of norwogonin (via SbF8H) [28, 29].

occurrences.source_citation: Zhao Q, Zhang Y, Wang G, et al. (2016) A specialized flavone biosynthetic pathway has evolved in the medicinal plant, Scutellaria baicalensis. Sci Adv 2:e1501780
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke also Leaf max 40 ppm. Zhao 2016 (Sci Adv): FNSII-2 in roots synthesises '4′-deoxyRSFs, such as chrysin and wogonin ...'. KNApSAcK C00003794. Costine 2022 found chrysin not detected in most tissues. | Basis as recorded: ppm as listed by Duke (basis not stated per row; for 'Essent. Oil' parts it is ppm of the oil, 10000 ppm = 1 %) Basis (fresh/dry weight) not stated by the source; excluded from /compare until confirmed.

pharmacology.mechanism: Described as a naturally occurring benzodiazepine-receptor ligand with anticonvulsant properties in animals [37].

evidence.outcome_summary: Reviewed as a natural BZD-receptor ligand with anticonvulsant effect in animals.

compound.teaching_note: Chrysin is the pathway's starting flavone; most of it is converted onward, so there is little left to measure [24, 28].
gaps: S. lateriflora row dropped (trace, no database record).
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
